newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK CBANK DRAFT ALLOWS FOREIGN BANKS REAL ESTATE.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK CBANK DRAFT ALLOWS FOREIGN BANKS REAL ESTATE.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Friday it had approved a draft law effectively allowing Slovak branches of foreign banks to buy real estate in Slovakia.
It also said in a statement that it had proposed ending the current 60,000 crown annual limit on foreign currency purchases by citizens.

"The NBS governing board on Friday approved a draft amendment to the foreign exchange law that should allow Slovak branches of foreign banks to purchase Slovak real estate," the statement, issued after a regular governing board meeting, said.
The NBS now must present the law to the parliament, but did not say when it would do so. Nor did it say when it proposed for the new law to become effective.
The NBS also approved an unspecified measure that set certain conditions when entities would not be required to ask for foreign exchange permission to trade foreign securities.
In addition, it also sets conditions for instances when central bank permission would not be needed to issue foreign securities to be traded on the Slovak market.
The statement did not give further details and bank officials were not immediately available for additional comment on the prepared measures.
The statement did not elaborate on the removal of the currency limit.
The NBS governing board also approved an analysis of development of central bank's hard currency reserves in 1996.
The document said central bank reserves rose by $54.6 million last year -- boosted mainly by a surplus from the foreign exchange fixing. As of December 31, 1996, foreign reserves $3.473 billion.
